thesis: The enterprise has decentralized application creation. It now needs to centralize how those applications are secured, operated, and governed.

methodology.heading: Methodology
methodology.body: This case tests the risk of doing nothing, the cost of delay or building internally, and the value created and risk mitigated by Vercel. It uses known facts and outcomes the business can measure directly, not a broad productivity estimate.

sections.heading: A prototype creates potential. A governed application creates value.

paragraphs.text: company-owned, securely connected, reliably operated, observable, and transferable.
Without those properties, more creation means more unsupported software, unmanaged access, and hidden cost.
The objective is to make each application usable, secure, and supportable without turning it into another central IT project.

sections.heading: Citizen developers will host their applications. The question is where.

paragraphs.text: Employees across the business already create applications with AI coding tools.
Without an approved route to production, useful applications remain prototypes, wait for central IT, or move to personal accounts and public services.
Each outcome destroys value: AI coding licences produce less usable software, specialist demand grows, or ownership, credentials, access, and cost move outside company control.
Building internally shifts the same burden to central IT. It must assemble and continuously operate identity, secrets, deployment, scaling, observability, cost controls, recovery, audit, and support.

sections.callout: Doing nothing is not neutral. It makes fragmented hosting the default and increases the estate the company must later discover, migrate, and govern.

sections.heading: One platform turns citizen development into a governed operating model.

paragraphs.text: Vercel is the managed platform for building, running, and governing applications and AI agents. Builders receive a direct route to production. Administrators retain ownership, visibility, and control. Vercel operates and supports the underlying platform.

advantages.value: Target 10× faster delivery of applications and agents, with no setup or infrastructure expertise required from builders.
advantages.risk: Avoids specialist queues, repeated setup, and valuable AI-created applications remaining on laptops.
advantages.fact: Measure time to first use, handoffs, and specialist hours per application.

advantages.value: Applications can use approved company systems through managed credentials and each user’s existing permissions.
advantages.risk: Prevents copied credentials, excessive access, and a bespoke integration project for every application.
advantages.fact: Measure integration lead time, access exceptions, and credentials exposed to builders.

advantages.value: Applications and agents deploy with zero configuration and scale with demand on one production platform.
advantages.risk: Avoids per-application Kubernetes work, idle capacity, fragmented runtime stacks, and specialist staffing.
advantages.fact: Measure platform hours, runtime services, and infrastructure cost per application.

advantages.value: Ownership, access, deployments, agent activity, usage, and cost remain visible in one control plane.
advantages.risk: Contains shadow IT, unknown owners, uncontrolled actions, fragmented audit evidence, and abnormal spend.
advantages.fact: Measure ownership and policy coverage, audit effort, and time to contain abnormal usage.

advantages.value: Shared operations, platform updates, and Enterprise Support let central IT govern the fleet instead of supporting every stack.
advantages.risk: Prevents each application becoming a separate maintenance, security, recovery, and support liability.
advantages.fact: Measure internal escalations, recovery time, maintenance hours, and applications per administrator.

outcomes.heading: Value
outcomes.body: Every new application reuses the same production path, integrations, controls, and operating model. More AI-created applications can reach users while repeated setup, waiting, and central support grow more slowly than the application estate.

outcomes.heading: Risk
outcomes.body: Company ownership, identity, auditability, spend visibility, recovery, and support become defaults. Governance no longer depends on every citizen developer assembling these controls correctly.
